definition_en: to imitate the appearance or conditions of something, sometimes in order to deceive
core_image: 飞行模拟舱里，仪表和真飞机一样转动，但窗外只是一块屏幕
scene: 飞行训练中心，学员在模拟舱里练习迫降。教官说：The simulator can simulate an engine failure at 30,000 feet.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 simulate 是「模拟、仿真」（第 2、4 个义项：用模型重现真实条件）；句意：模拟器可以模拟三万英尺高空的发动机失效。图中可辨识物件：模拟舱、仪表盘、球形屏幕、教员座椅。

senses.title: To pretend: putting on a false front
senses.titleCN: 假装：摆出不真实的样子
senses.definition: to pretend to have a feeling, illness or quality that one does not really have
senses.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种实际并不存在的情感、疾病或品质
senses.example: He simulated illness to avoid the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 他装病以逃避考试。
senses.why: Latin simulare could mean both 'to make like' and 'to feign'. The second sense survives: the outer surface is copied, while the inner state is missing. Simulation is a likeness with no substance behind it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 simulare 既可表示“使相像”，也可表示“假装”。第二个义项活了下来：外层表面被复制，而内在状态缺席。假装是一种背后没有实质的相似。

senses.title: To reproduce real conditions
senses.definition: to create conditions that copy the important features of a real situation, usually for study or training
senses.definitionCN: 创造复制了真实情境重要特征的条件，通常用于研究或训练
senses.example: The chamber simulates the pressure at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这个舱室模拟高海拔的气压。
senses.why: Here the copy is honest: the aim is not to deceive but to reproduce. Engineers keep the variables that matter and drop the rest, so the model can be tested safely.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制是诚实的：目的不是欺骗，而是重现。工程师保留真正重要的变量，舍弃其余部分，从而能安全地测试模型。

senses.title: To imitate an appearance or sound
senses.definition: to copy the look, sound or manner of something so that it resembles the original
senses.definitionCN: 复制某物的外观、声音或举止，使其像原物
senses.example: The actor simulated the old man's walk.
senses.exampleCN: 演员模仿了那位老人的步态。
senses.why: The Latin verb was used for making a copy of a thing. In this sense the imitation is visible and often skilful, and the question of deceit does not arise.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本就用于“给某物做一个复本”。在这个义项里，模仿是可见的、常常很技巧性，是否欺骗的问题并不出现。

senses.title: Computer simulation
senses.definition: to run a model on a computer so that it reproduces the behaviour of a real system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上运行模型，使其重现真实系统的行为
senses.example: The program simulates how heat spreads through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 该程序模拟热量如何在墙体中传导。
senses.why: A computer can carry a model through thousands of steps that would be too slow or too dangerous to run in reality. Simulation here means letting a formal description act out the process.
senses.whyCN: 计算机能把模型推进成千上万步，而在现实中跑这些步骤要么太慢、要么太危险。这里的仿真，就是让一份形式化描述“演”出整个过程。

senses.title: Training by simulated practice
senses.definition: to let a learner practise in an artificial setting that reproduces the pressures of the real task
senses.definitionCN: 让学习者在复现真实任务压力的人造环境中练习
senses.example: Pilots train on simulators before flying real aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在驾驶真飞机之前先在模拟器上训练。
senses.why: The point of simulated flight is that mistakes are cheap. The copy is close enough to transfer skill, yet detached enough to absorb failure.
senses.whyCN: 模拟飞行的意义在于犯错的代价很低。这个复本足够接近真实，使技能可以迁移；又足够脱离真实，使失败可以被吸收。

senses.title: To feign an attitude
senses.definition: to display an emotion or interest that one does not feel, usually for social reasons
senses.definitionCN: 表现出并未真正感受到的情绪或兴趣，通常出于社交原因
senses.example: She simulated interest in the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 她假装对讲座感兴趣。
senses.why: Social life often requires the surface of an emotion without its substance. The word marks exactly that gap: the visible sign is produced, the inner state is not.
senses.whyCN: 社交生活常常需要情绪的表面，而不需要它的实质。这个词标记的正是那道缝隙：可见的信号被制造出来，内在状态却不存在。

senses.title: To model an outcome
senses.definition: to use a model to work out what would happen under given conditions, before the event occurs
senses.definitionCN: 用模型推算出在给定条件下会发生什么，且发生在事件之前
senses.example: Economists simulated the effect of the tax cut.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家模拟了减税的效果。
senses.why: The model is a stand-in that can be pushed ahead of reality. Simulating an outcome is a way of trying the future at low cost.
senses.whyCN: 模型是现实的替身，可以被推到现实之前。模拟结果，就是用低成本的方式先“试一遍”未来。

senses.title: Simulating biological conditions
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, to reproduce the chemical or physical conditions of a living system
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，重现生命系统的化学或物理条件
senses.example: The device simulates the acidity of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该装置模拟胃部的酸度。
senses.why: Living systems are hard to open and hard to control. A simulated environment keeps the relevant parameters while removing the complexity that would confound the experiment.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统难以打开、也难以控制。模拟环境保留相关参数，同时去掉会干扰实验的复杂性。

senses.title: Simulated: the adjective of the artificial
senses.definition: the past participle works as an adjective meaning 'made to resemble something real, and not real itself'
senses.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为“被做成像真的、但本身并非真的”
senses.example: The aircraft landed on a simulated runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落在一条模拟跑道上。
senses.why: Once the participle becomes an adjective, the 'as if' is packed into a single word: simulated leather, simulated flavour, simulated emergency. The likeness is the point, and the absence of the original is understood.
senses.whyCN: 当分词变成形容词，“仿佛”就被压缩进一个词里：simulated leather、simulated flavour、simulated emergency。相似本身就是重点，而原物的缺席则是不言自明的。

intro.en: Simulate comes from Latin simulare 'to make like, imitate, represent', built on similis 'like'. English first used it in the 1620s for pretending; the technical sense 'reproduce conditions with a model' is a 20th-century development.
intro.cn: simulate 来自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、再现”，建立在 similis“像”之上。英语在 17 世纪 20 年代最早用它表示“假装”；“用模型重现条件”的技术义则是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, resembling'. It is the adjective behind the whole family, and its older relative semol 'together' points to PIE *sem- 'one, together'.
items.cn: similis 意为“相像的”。它是整个词族背后的形容词，其更早的亲属 semol“一起”指向原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”。

items.en: Simulare meant 'to make like, copy, imitate, represent', and also 'to pretend'. The verb could describe an artist copying a face or a person faking a feeling.
items.cn: simulare 意为“使相像、复制、模仿、再现”，也可表示“假装”。这个动词既能描述画家复制一张脸，也能描述一个人伪造一种情感。

items.en: The past participle simulatus 'made like, imitated, feigned' supplied the stem for the English verb. The Latin supine form simulatum also underlies the noun simulation.
items.cn: 过去分词 simulatus“被弄得相像的、被模仿的、被假装的”为英语动词提供了词干。拉丁语动名词形式 simulatum 也是名词 simulation 的基础。

items.en: English simulate is first recorded in the 1620s with the sense 'to feign, pretend'. It was either a back-formation from simulation or a direct borrowing of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 英语 simulate 最早记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“假装、装作”。它要么是从 simulation 逆构而来，要么是直接借用了拉丁语分词。

items.en: The modern technical sense 'to imitate the working of a system, especially with a model or computer' is recorded from the mid-20th century (c. 1947), alongside the growth of simulators.
items.cn: 现代技术义“模仿某一系统的运作，尤指用模型或计算机”记录于 20 世纪中期（约 1947），与模拟器的兴起同步。

items.en: Simulation, simulator and simulated now cover engineering, medicine, economics and games. The old polarity survives: the copy may be offered as a tool, or offered as a deception.
items.cn: simulation、simulator、simulated 如今覆盖工程、医学、经济学与游戏。旧的二元性仍然存在：这个复本既可以作为工具提供，也可以作为骗局提供。

note.en: The look-alike group is the simul- family; the near-meaning group compares verbs of copying and pretending. Watch the difference between an honest model and a deliberate lie.
note.cn: 形近组是 simul- 词族；近义组比较表示复制与假装的动词。注意“诚实的模型”与“有意的谎言”之间的差别。

entries.definition: the act or result of simulating; a model that reproduces a real process. It is the noun of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 模拟的行为或结果；重现真实过程的模型。它是 simulate 的名词。

entries.definition: a device or program that simulates conditions for training or study. It is the thing that does the simulating.
entries.definitionCN: 为训练或研究而模拟条件的装置或程序。它是执行模拟的那个东西。

entries.definition: to hide one's real feelings by pretending the opposite. The prefix dis- reverses the direction of the pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过装作相反的样子来掩盖真实情感。前缀 dis- 反转了伪装的方向。

entries.definition: to copy someone's actions or manner, often to learn or to entertain. It does not imply deception.
entries.definitionCN: 复制他人的行为或举止，常用于学习或娱乐。它不暗示欺骗。

entries.definition: to copy the sound or movement of something, often in a playful or exaggerated way.
entries.definitionCN: 复制某物的声音或动作，常带有戏仿或夸张。

entries.definition: to pretend to have a feeling or condition. It is close to the oldest sense of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种情感或状况。它接近 simulate 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to try to equal or surpass someone by imitating their success. It adds striving, not pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过模仿他人的成功来试图赶上或超越。它增加了努力，而不是伪装。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a flight simulator, a fake cough, a computer model of heat, a simulated runway.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：飞行模拟器、假装的咳嗽、热的计算机模型、模拟跑道。

normal.en: Similis is 'like': to simulate is to make something look or behave like the real thing.
normal.cn: similis 就是“像”：simulate 就是让某物看起来或表现得像真的。

normal.en: A flight simulator copies the cockpit but not the sky: the relevant parts are real, the danger is not.
normal.cn: 飞行模拟器复制了驾驶舱，却没有复制天空：相关部分是真实的，危险则不是。

normal.en: Simulate an illness is to fake it; simulate a climate is to model it. One deceives, the other studies.
normal.cn: simulate an illness 是装病；simulate a climate 是建模。前者骗人，后者研究。

normal.en: The noun pair: simulation is the process, simulator is the machine.
normal.cn: 名词配对：simulation 是过程，simulator 是机器。

normal.en: Simulated leather, simulated flavour: the adjective tells you the real material is absent.
normal.cn: simulated leather、simulated flavour：这个形容词告诉你真正的材料并不在场。

abstract.en: One schema: LIKE → COPY → PRETEND → REPRODUCE → MODEL → TEST.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：像 → 复制 → 假装 → 重现 → 建模 → 检验。

abstract.en: Word-family check: similar (adj.) → simulate (v.) → simulation (n.) → simulator (n.) → simulated (adj.).
abstract.cn: 词族检查：similar（形）→ simulate（动）→ simulation（名）→ simulator（名）→ simulated（形）。

abstract.en: Contrast: imitate copies behaviour, mimic copies sound, feign fakes a state, emulate copies in order to rival.
abstract.cn: 对照：imitate 复制行为，mimic 复制声音，feign 伪造状态，emulate 为竞争而复制。

examples.en: The program simulates how the virus spreads through a city.
examples.cn: 该程序模拟病毒如何在一座城市中传播。

examples.en: He simulated a headache to leave the meeting early.
examples.cn: 他假装头痛，以便提前离开会议。

examples.en: The astronauts trained in a simulated weightless environment.
examples.cn: 宇航员在模拟失重环境中训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西米尤勒特”——西米（粒）尤（其）勒（住）特（像）→ 把东西勒成一样 → simulate 模拟、假装

root: 源自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、假装”，由 similis“相像的”派生；过去分词 simulatus 进入英语。核心是“做出一个像真的复本”，既可用于诚实的建模，也可用于欺骗性的假装。

sensesIntro.en: Simulate starts from a copy. The oldest sense is pretence: a person fakes an illness or an interest. The same act becomes respectable when the copy is meant to teach or to predict: an altitude chamber reproduces pressure, a computer runs a model, a pilot practises on a simulator, an economist tries the future before it arrives. The adjective simulated then carries the whole idea in one word: made to resemble something real, and not real itself.
sensesIntro.cn: simulate 的起点是一个复本。最古老的义项是伪装：一个人装病、装感兴趣。当复本被用来教学或预测时，同一个动作就变得正当：高压舱重现气压，计算机跑模型，飞行员在模拟器上练习，经济学家在未来到来之前先试一遍。形容词 simulated 则用一个词承载整个观念：被做成像真的，而本身并非真的。

core.en: Making a likeness: copying a surface, a condition or a process, with or without intent to deceive.
core.cn: 制造相似：复制表面、条件或过程，可能有意欺骗，也可能没有。

branches.en: PRETENCE: faking an illness, and faking an attitude, where the inner state is missing.
branches.cn: 伪装：装病与装态度，内在状态缺席。

branches.en: IMITATION: copying a walk, a voice or a manner for display.
branches.cn: 模仿：为展示而复制步态、声音或举止。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: recreating real physical or biological conditions for study.
branches.cn: 重现：为研究而再造真实的物理或生理条件。

branches.en: MODELLING: running a system or an outcome through a model, often on a computer.
branches.cn: 建模：用模型推演系统或结果，常在计算机上运行。

branches.en: TRAINING AND ARTIFICE: simulated practice, and the adjective for things that only resemble the real.
branches.cn: 训练与人造：模拟练习，以及表示“只是像真的”的形容词。

intro.en: Simulate sits in the simil-/simul- family. The items below move from the Latin verb through the modern technical nouns to the adjective of artifice.
intro.cn: simulate 位于 simil-/simul- 词族中。下列条目从拉丁动词出发，经过现代技术名词，到达表示“人造”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' gives simulare 'make like', whose participle simulatus supplies English simulate. Simulacrum adds the idea of a mere image or shadow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis“像”派生出 simulare“使相像”，其分词 simulatus 提供英语 simulate。simulacrum 则加入“仅是影像或影子”的意思。

items.meaning: the act or result of simulating
items.example: The simulation took six hours to run.
items.exampleCN: 这次仿真运行了六个小时。

items.meaning: a device or program that simulates
items.exampleCN: 模拟器重现驾驶舱条件。

items.example: They tested the material in simulated sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 他们在模拟阳光下测试该材料。

items.meaningCN: 模拟性的；有模仿作用的
items.example: The game has a simulative function.
items.exampleCN: 这款游戏具有模拟功能。

items.meaning: to conceal one's feelings by pretence

items.exampleCN: 她的镇定完全是装出来的。
这个寓言通过比喻起作用。

items.meaning: an image or imitation that lacks substance
items.meaningCN: 影像；幻影；徒有其表的东西
items.example: The town was a simulacrum of a real city.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇只是一座真实城市的仿像。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被弄得相像的；被假装的

definition_zh: 模拟；仿真；模拟实验；假装；模拟装置
definition_en: the imitation of a real process or situation, often by a model or computer, for study or training
core_image: 一间飞行训练舱里，屏幕上是云层，座椅随气流轻轻抖动
scene: 这里指「模拟」。 Pilots train in a simulation before they ever fly the real aircraft.
sceneCN: 这里 simulation 指「仿真训练装置」（第 3 个义项：用模型复现真实操作环境以供练习）；飞行员先在模拟舱训练，再上真机。图中可辨识物件：驾驶舱、投影云层、操纵杆、教员台。

pos.zh: 模拟；仿真；模拟实验；假装；模拟装置（可数或不可数，指装置或一次实验时用复数 simulations）

senses.title: Imitating a process
senses.titleCN: 模拟过程：用模型复现真实运行
senses.definition: the imitation of the behaviour of a real system by a model, often a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 用模型（常为计算机程序）再现真实系统的行为
senses.example: The simulation reproduced twenty years of erosion in four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这次模拟用四小时再现了二十年的侵蚀。
senses.why: Latin simulatio meant 'a copying or feigning', from simulare 'to make like', built on similis 'similar'; the noun begins as 'making something like'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 simulatio 意为「模仿或假装」，出自 simulare「使相似」，而后者基于 similis「相似的」；这个名词的起点是「使某物相像」。

senses.title: A model's run
senses.titleCN: 一次仿真运算：模型跑出的一组结果
senses.definition: one complete run of a model producing a set of predicted outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 模型完整运行一次所产出的一组预测结果
senses.example: We ran a thousand simulations to estimate the range of sea level rise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑了一千次模拟来估计海平面上升的区间。
senses.why: Countability arrived with computing: each run is a separate event, so the abstract noun became countable.
senses.whyCN: 可数性随计算而来：每次运行都是独立事件，于是抽象名词变得可数。

senses.title: A training device
senses.titleCN: 训练用仿真装置：可反复练习的假环境
senses.definition: an apparatus that reproduces conditions for practice or testing
senses.definitionCN: 复现某种条件以供练习或测试的装置
senses.example: The hospital bought a simulation for practising emergency births.
senses.exampleCN: 医院购置了一套用于演练紧急分娩的模拟装置。
senses.why: The abstract act turned into a concrete object: the thing that performs the imitation is called a simulation.
senses.whyCN: 抽象动作转为具体物件：执行这种模仿的东西就被称为 simulation。

senses.title: Pretending an emotion
senses.titleCN: 假装：做出并非真心的表现
senses.definition: the act of feigning a feeling or condition one does not have
senses.definitionCN: 装作拥有某种并不真正具备的情感或状态
senses.example: His grief was simulation, and everyone at the table knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的悲痛是假装的，桌上每个人都知道。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: simulatio in Latin covered feigning, and English kept it alongside the technical use.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：拉丁 simulatio 本就涵盖假装，英语把这个义项与技术义一并保留。

senses.title: Simulation in statistics
senses.titleCN: 统计模拟：用随机抽样近似结果
senses.definition: in statistics, generating random samples to approximate a distribution or probability
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指生成随机样本来近似某一分布或概率
senses.example: Monte Carlo simulation estimates the integral without solving it.
senses.exampleCN: 蒙特卡洛模拟无需解出积分即可估计其值。
senses.why: Statistics uses imitation as a computational strategy: when the answer cannot be derived, it is acted out many times.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把「模仿」当作计算策略：当答案无法推导时，就把它反复演出来。

senses.title: Simulation of a physical system
senses.titleCN: 物理系统仿真：在方程中预演现实
senses.definition: in engineering and physics, solving a system's equations to predict its behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 工程与物理中通过求解系统方程来预测其行为
senses.example: The bridge design was tested by simulation before any steel was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 桥的设计在切任何钢材之前先经过仿真测试。
senses.why: Engineering extended the word to numerical prediction: a cheap copy of the structure runs before the costly real one exists.
senses.whyCN: 工程把这个词延伸到数值预测：在昂贵的实物存在之前，先让一个廉价的复制品跑起来。

senses.title: Simulation of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 行为模拟：让智能体模仿真实行为
senses.definition: in social science and computing, modelling the actions of people or agents
senses.definitionCN: 社会科学与计算中，对人或智能体行为的建模
senses.example: The crowd simulation showed where bottlenecks would form.
senses.exampleCN: 人群模拟显示出瓶颈会在哪里形成。
senses.why: The object imitated shifted from nature to people: agents are given rules and their behaviour is acted out.
senses.whyCN: 被模仿的对象从自然转向人：给智能体设定规则，再演出的行为。

senses.title: Simulation as deception
senses.definition: a false appearance deliberately kept up to mislead
senses.definitionCN: 为误导而刻意维持的虚假外表
senses.example: The ceasefire was a simulation of peace that lasted three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那次停火是一场维持了三周的和平假象。
senses.why: Feigning enlarged to public events: what is put on for show, without substance, is called simulation.
senses.whyCN: 假装扩大到公共事件：为展示而摆出、并无实质的东西，被称为 simulation。

intro.en: Simulation comes from Latin simulatio, from simulare 'to make like, to imitate', built on similis 'similar'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: simulation 出自拉丁 simulatio，源自 simulare「使相似、模仿」，基于 similis「相似的」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin similis meant 'like, similar'. It is well recorded, and it also underlies similis-based words such as resemble and similar; its deeper origin is disputed.
items.cn: 拉丁 similis 意为「相像的、相似的」。记录充分，也支撑 resemble、similar 等词；其更深来源有争议。

items.en: The verb simulare meant 'to make like, to copy, and also to feign'. The feigning sense was present from early on, which is why the noun carries both imitation and pretence.
items.cn: 动词 simulare 意为「使相像、复制」，也表示「假装」。假装义很早就存在，因此这个名词同时承载「模仿」与「作假」。

items.en: The noun simulatio covered 'a likeness, an imitation, a feigning'. Classical usage leans toward the negative, pretence.
items.cn: 名词 simulatio 涵盖「相似、模仿、假装」。古典用法偏向负面，即「作假」。

items.en: English simulation appears in the Middle Ages through French, first meaning 'pretence'. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 simulation 经法语于中世纪出现，初义为「假装」。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: From the mid-twentieth century simulation became primarily technical: a model imitating a system, and later a device reproducing conditions for training.
items.cn: 自 20 世纪中叶起，simulation 主要成为技术词：模型模仿系统，后又指复现条件以供训练的装置。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date is uncertain; the origin of similis before its 'like' sense is debated and any Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：英语首见年代存疑；similis 在「相像」义之前的来源有争议，任何印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that differ in part of speech; the second holds near-synonyms for imitation or for a model.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，区别在词性；第二组是表示模仿或模型的近义词。

entries.definition: To imitate or feign. It names the act; simulation is the act as a thing or the device that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 模拟或假装。它命名动作；simulation 则是作为事物的动作，或执行该动作的装置。

entries.definition: Describes something artificial made to resemble the real thing, as in simulated leather. It is a property, not a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为仿照真品而造的人造物，如 simulated leather。它是属性，而非程序。

entries.definition: The device that runs the imitation. Simulation can also mean the device, but simulator is the precise term.
entries.definitionCN: 执行模仿的装置。simulation 也可指装置，但 simulator 是更精确的说法。

entries.definition: Means 'alike'. It shares similis but makes no claim about imitation or modelling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「相似的」。它同出 similis，但与模仿或建模无关。

entries.definition: A simplified representation of a system. A model is the thing used; a simulation is the running of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对系统的简化表示。模型是被使用的对象；模拟则是让它运行起来。

entries.definition: The act of copying something, often with the implication of inferiority. Simulation is neutral in technical use.
entries.definitionCN: 复制某物的行为，常含「次一等」的意味。simulation 在技术语境中是中性的。

entries.definition: Copying in order to equal or surpass. It carries rivalry, while simulation need not compete.
entries.definitionCN: 为追平或超越而仿效。它带有竞争意味，而 simulation 不必涉及竞争。

entries.definition: An exact copy or a repeated experiment. It stresses fidelity, while simulation stresses a working imitation.
entries.definitionCN: 精确复制或重复实验。它强调忠实度，而 simulation 强调可运行的模仿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: similis 'similar' + -atio: making something like the real thing.
normal.cn: similis「相似的」+ -atio：把某物做得像真的。

normal.en: The family runs similar, simulate, simulated, simulation, simulator, dissimulate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 similar、simulate、simulated、simulation、simulator、dissimulate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: computer simulation, simulation model, flight simulation, run a simulation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：计算机模拟、仿真模型、飞行模拟、运行一次模拟。

normal.en: The same noun covers the act, one run, and the machine that does it.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既覆盖动作、一次运行，也覆盖执行它的机器。

normal.en: The Latin noun already meant 'pretence', which is why the word can still accuse someone of faking.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词本就含「假装」，因此这个词至今仍可用来指责作假。

abstract.en: Picture a cockpit on the ground, with clouds painted on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一间留在地面的驾驶舱，云层画在屏幕上。

abstract.en: Picture a scale model of a bridge bending under tiny weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥梁的缩尺模型在小砝码下弯曲。

abstract.en: Picture an actor crying on cue, with no grief behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一名演员按提示落泪，背后并无悲伤。

examples.en: The climate simulation predicted a wetter winter for the region.
examples.cn: 这次气候模拟预测该地区冬季将更湿润。

examples.en: Medical students practise on a simulation before touching a patient.
examples.cn: 医学生在接触病人之前先在模拟装置上练习。

examples.en: Her calm was a simulation that lasted until the door closed.
examples.cn: 她的镇定是装出来的，一直撑到门关上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「simil（相似）+ ation（行为）」——做出相似的东西 → simulation 模拟、仿真

root: 拉丁 similis「相似的」→ simulare「使相似、模仿、假装」→ simulatio「模仿；假装」→ 英语 simulation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one imitation: something is made to behave like the real thing, and that copy can be a run of a model, a training machine, a statistical trick or a lie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次模仿展开：某物被做得像真的，而这个复制品可以是一次模型运算、一台训练机器、一种统计手段，也可以是一句谎言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cockpit on the ground with painted clouds and a shaking seat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间留在地面的驾驶舱，云层是画上去的，座椅在抖。

branches.en: TECHNICAL IMITATION: a model reproduces a real process, whether natural or engineered.
branches.cn: 技术模仿：模型再现真实过程，无论自然的还是工程的。

branches.en: COUNTED RUNS: each execution is a simulation, and random runs approximate an answer.
branches.cn: 可数的运行：每次执行都是一次模拟，随机运行可逼近答案。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND AGENTS: the device imitates conditions, and agents imitate behaviour.
branches.cn: 装置与智能体：装置模仿条件，智能体模仿行为。

branches.en: FEIGNING: the oldest Latin layer, where the copy is worn as a mask.
branches.cn: 假装：最古老的拉丁层，复制品被当作面具戴上。

branches.en: PUBLIC PRETENCE: feigning scaled up to events presented as real.
branches.cn: 公共假象：假装被放大为被呈现为真实的事件。

intro.en: Simulation is a Latin likeness stem with a verb-forming suffix and an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: simulation 是拉丁「相似」词干加动词化后缀与动作名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' gives simulare 'to make like'; -atio turns the verb into the action noun simulatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis「相像」产生 simulare「使相像」；-atio 把动词转为动作名词 simulatio。

items.example: The simulation took six hours to run.
items.exampleCN: 这次模拟运行了六小时。

items.example: The simulator logged every control input.
items.exampleCN: 模拟器记录了每一次操纵输入。

items.example: Similarity between the species is striking.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种的相似性很惊人。

items.meaning: to hide one's feelings by pretence
items.example: He dissimulated his anger with a smile.

definition_zh: 同时发生的；同时进行的；同时存在的；联立的
definition_en: happening or existing at exactly the same time
core_image: 两只秒表在同一刻同时按下，指针分毫不差
scene: 这里指「同时发生的」。 The two eruptions were simultaneous, though the volcanoes lie a thousand kilometres apart.
sceneCN: 这里 simultaneous 指「在同一时刻发生的」（第 1 个义项：时间上完全重合）；两座火山相距千里却同时喷发。图中可辨识物件：两座火山、同一时刻的钟面、震波记录、距离标尺。

pos.zh: 同时发生的；同时进行的；同时存在的；（方程）联立的（无比较级，需用 more simultaneous 表示程度）

senses.title: At the same moment
senses.titleCN: 同一时刻：两个事件时间重合
senses.definition: happening at exactly the same moment
senses.definitionCN: 在完全相同的时刻发生
senses.example: The two shots were simultaneous, and the race was called a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 两声枪响同时发生，比赛被判为平局。
senses.why: Latin simul 'at the same time' plus -aneus formed simultaneus, an adjective that simply states co-occurrence in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 simul「同时」加 -aneus 构成 simultaneus，这个形容词只是陈述时间上的共现。

senses.title: Running in parallel
senses.titleCN: 同时进行：两项活动并行推进
senses.definition: carried out at the same time rather than one after another
senses.definitionCN: 同时开展，而非一项接一项
senses.example: The two laboratories ran simultaneous trials on the same vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室对同一疫苗同时开展了试验。
senses.why: The same time relation applies to activities: parallel work is simultaneous work, and the contrast is with successive.
senses.whyCN: 同样的时间关系适用于活动：并行的工作就是同时的工作，其对照词是 successive（相继的）。

senses.title: Existing together
senses.titleCN: 同时存在：两种状态共处一时
senses.definition: existing at the same period, without one causing the other
senses.definitionCN: 在同一时期存在，彼此并无因果关系
senses.example: The two styles were simultaneous in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种风格在同一座城市同时存在。
senses.why: Coexistence extends the word from events to states: things need not start together to be simultaneous.
senses.whyCN: 共在把词义从事件延伸到状态：事物不必同时开始，也可以说是同时的。

senses.title: Simultaneous interpretation
senses.titleCN: 同声传译：说着听着一并进行
senses.definition: translation performed while the speaker is still talking
senses.definitionCN: 在说话人仍在讲话时进行的翻译
senses.example: He worked as a simultaneous interpreter at the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会议上担任同声传译。
senses.why: Conference technology made the word a fixed term: the interpreter's speech overlaps the speaker's, hence 'simultaneous'.
senses.whyCN: 会议技术让这个词成为固定术语：译员的说话与讲者重叠，故称「同时」。

senses.title: Simultaneous equations
senses.titleCN: 联立方程：必须一并求解的方程组
senses.definition: in mathematics, equations that must be satisfied by the same set of values
senses.definitionCN: 数学中必须由同一组数值同时满足的方程
senses.example: The pair of simultaneous equations has one solution.
senses.exampleCN: 这对联立方程只有一组解。
senses.why: Mathematics borrowed the word for conditions that must hold at once, in the same solution.
senses.whyCN: 数学借这个词表示必须同时成立的条件，即在同一组解中。

senses.title: Simultaneous in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理上的同时性：依参照系而定
senses.definition: in relativity, the property of two events occurring at the same time in a given frame of reference
senses.definitionCN: 相对论中，两事件在某一参照系下发生于同一时刻的性质
senses.example: Simultaneity is relative: two events simultaneous in one frame need not be in another.
senses.exampleCN: 同时性是相对的：在一个参照系中同时的两事件，在另一个参照系中未必同时。
senses.why: Relativity turned the everyday word into a frame-dependent quantity, one of the sharpest changes in its history.
senses.whyCN: 相对论把这个日常词变成依赖参照系的量，这是其历史上最剧烈的语义变化之一。

senses.title: Released at once
senses.titleCN: 同步发行：多地同一时间推出
senses.definition: of a product or broadcast, made available everywhere at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 指产品或节目在所有地方同一时间推出
senses.example: The film had a simultaneous release in forty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在四十个国家同步上映。
senses.why: Distribution uses the word to guarantee no market is ahead: the same clock governs every release.
senses.whyCN: 发行用这个词来保证没有市场抢先：同一个时钟支配每一次发布。

senses.title: Happening at once in a body
senses.titleCN: 体内同时发生：多个过程并存
senses.definition: in physiology, of processes occurring in the body at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 生理学中指体内多个过程在同一时间发生
senses.example: Digestion and absorption are partly simultaneous in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 在小肠中，消化与吸收部分是同时进行的。
senses.why: Biology applies the word to overlapping internal processes, where sequence is partial rather than strict.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个词用于体内重叠的过程，其间顺序只是部分的，而非严格的。

intro.en: Simultaneous is a Latin adjective built from simul 'at the same time' with the ending -aneus, probably through a later form simultaneus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: simultaneous 是拉丁形容词，由 simul「同时」加词尾 -aneus 构成，可能经由后世形式 simultaneus。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin simul is an adverb meaning 'at the same time, together'. It is common in classical prose and is related to similis 'like' in the sense of 'together, alike'.
items.cn: 拉丁 simul 是副词，意为「同时、一起」。古典散文中常见，与 similis「相像」在「一起、类似」的意味上相关。

items.en: Late Latin formed simultaneus 'existing at the same time'. The adjective is not classical, and its exact formation is uncertain: it may rest on a lost intermediate form.
items.cn: 后世拉丁构成 simultaneus「同时存在的」。这个形容词不属于古典拉丁，其确切构词存疑：可能建立在一个已失传的中间形式之上。

items.en: English simultaneous appears in the seventeenth century, in learned writing about time and motion. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 simultaneous 于 17 世纪出现，见于关于时间与运动的学术写作。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century technology gave the word fixed uses: simultaneous telegraphy, simultaneous interpreting, simultaneous release.
items.cn: 19、20 世纪的技术赋予该词固定用法：同时电报、同声传译、同步发行。

items.en: Einstein's 1905 paper on relativity made simultaneity a frame-dependent relation, and the word became a technical term in physics.
items.cn: 爱因斯坦 1905 年的相对论论文把同时性变成依赖参照系的关系，这个词由此成为物理学术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (root disputed): the formation of simultaneus is not securely explained and may involve a lost intermediate. Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：simultaneus 的构词方式尚无确凿解释，可能涉及已失传的中间形式；来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：英语首见年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close but state a different time relation; the second holds near-synonyms of co-occurrence.
note.cn: 第一组是形近但表达不同时间关系的词；第二组是表示共现的近义词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of verbs: the two events happened simultaneously. The adjective modifies nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，用于动词：两件事同时发生。形容词则修饰名词。

entries.definition: Means 'unplanned, arising from inner impulse'. It comes from Latin sponte 'of one's own accord' and has nothing to do with time.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「自发的、出于内在冲动的」。它出自拉丁 sponte「自愿」，与时间无关。

entries.definition: Means 'occurring in an instant, with no duration'. Two instantaneous events may still be at different times.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「瞬间发生、没有持续时间的」。两个瞬时事件仍可能处于不同时刻。

entries.definition: Following in sequence. It is the direct contrast: simultaneous events overlap, successive ones do not.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序相继。它是直接的反义对照：同时的事件重叠，相继的事件不重叠。

entries.definition: Happening over the same period, not necessarily at the same instant. It is the usual word for long processes running in parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时期发生，不必在同一瞬间。它是描述长期过程并行的常用词。

entries.definition: Happening at the same rate and in step. It stresses coordination of timing, while simultaneous stresses the same moment.
entries.definitionCN: 以相同速率并保持同步地发生。它强调时间上的协调，而 simultaneous 强调同一时刻。

entries.definition: Occurring at the same time, often by chance. It suggests coincidence, while simultaneous is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 同一时间发生，常含偶然之意。它暗示巧合，而 simultaneous 是中性的。

entries.definition: Developing side by side without meeting. It stresses independence of two tracks, not exact timing.
entries.definitionCN: 并排发展而不相交。它强调两条路径的独立性，而非精确的时点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin simul 'at the same time' + -aneus: the adjective of co-occurrence.
normal.cn: 拉丁 simul「同时」+ -aneus：表示共现的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs simultaneous, simultaneously, simultaneity, simulcast.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 simultaneous、simultaneously、simultaneity、simulcast。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: simultaneous interpretation, simultaneous equations, simultaneous release.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：同声传译、联立方程、同步发行。

normal.en: The key contrast is successive: simultaneous overlaps, successive queues up.
normal.cn: 关键对照是 successive：同时的重叠，相继的排队。

normal.en: In relativity, simultaneity is relative to the observer's frame, which is why the noun is simultaneity, not 'same time'.
normal.cn: 在相对论中，同时性相对于观察者的参照系，这正是名词取 simultaneity 而非「同一时间」的原因。

abstract.en: Picture two stopwatches clicked by the same thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象两只秒表被同一根拇指按下。

abstract.en: Picture two trains entering a station from opposite ends at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象两列火车在同一秒从车站两端驶入。

abstract.en: Picture an interpreter speaking while the original voice is still in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象译员开口时，原声仍在房间里回荡。

examples.en: The two experiments were simultaneous, so the results could be compared directly.
examples.cn: 两项实验同时进行，因此结果可以直接比较。

examples.en: Simultaneous translation let the visiting scientists follow the lecture.
examples.cn: 同声传译让来访的科学家能跟上讲座。

examples.en: In one frame the flashes are simultaneous; in another they are not.
examples.cn: 在某个参照系中两道闪光是同时的，在另一个参照系中则不是。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「simul（同时）+ taneous（……的）」——同一时间发生的 → simultaneous 同时的

root: 拉丁 simul「同时」→ 后世拉丁 simultaneus「同时存在的」→ 英语 simultaneous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one clock reading: two things occupy the same moment, and the word can describe events, activities, styles, equations, releases or a frame-dependent physical relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次读时展开：两样东西占据同一时刻，这个词既可描述事件、活动、风格、方程、发行，也可描述依赖参照系的物理关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stopwatches clicked by the same thumb.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只秒表被同一根拇指按下。

branches.en: SAME INSTANT: the plainest sense, two events at one moment.
branches.cn: 同一瞬间：最朴素的义项，两事件在一个时刻。

branches.en: OVERLAP: activities and states share a stretch of time without one causing the other.
branches.cn: 重叠：活动与状态共享一段时间，彼此并无因果。

branches.en: TECHNICAL OVERLAP: interpreting and release scheduling both require exact co-timing.
branches.cn: 技术性重叠：同传与发行排期都要求精确的同刻。

branches.en: MATHEMATICAL: conditions that must hold in one and the same solution.
branches.cn: 数学：必须在同一组解中成立的条件。

branches.en: PHYSICS AND BODY: simultaneity becomes frame-dependent, or describes overlapping internal processes.
branches.cn: 物理与身体：同时性变为依赖参照系，或描述体内重叠的过程。

intro.en: Simultaneous is a Latin adverb of time turned into an adjective by the ending -aneus; it has no prefix and no productive suffix of its own.
intro.cn: simultaneous 是拉丁时间副词经 -aneus 词尾转为形容词；它没有前缀，也没有自身能产的独立后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin simul 'at the same time' supplies the stem; -aneus is a Latin adjective ending seen in words such as extraneus and spontaneus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 simul「同时」提供词干；-aneus 是拉丁形容词词尾，见于 extraneus、spontaneus 等词。

items.example: She read and took notes simultaneously.

items.meaning: the state of being at the same time
items.exampleCN: 相对论把同时性视为相对的。

items.meaning: a broadcast sent on several channels at once
items.meaningCN: 同时通过多个频道播出的节目
items.example: The concert was a simulcast on radio and television.
items.exampleCN: 这场音乐会通过广播与电视同步播出。

items.example: The Latin adverb survives only in compounds.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁副词只保留在复合词中。

items.example: Remove extraneous detail from the report.
items.exampleCN: 删去报告中无关的细节。

items.example: Two concurrent studies reached the same result.
items.exampleCN: 两项并行研究得出了相同结果。

latinEntries.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of

definition_en: at the same time, with two or more things happening together
core_image: 两只手在同一秒按下两个不同的开关
scene: 这里指「同时地」。 The system updates the two databases simultaneously, so neither can lag behind.
sceneCN: 这里 simultaneously 指「在同一时刻一并地」（第 1 个义项：多个动作时间完全重合）；系统同时更新两个数据库，两者都不会落后。图中可辨识物件：两个数据库图标、同步指示、时钟、连线。

senses.title: At one and the same moment
senses.titleCN: 同一时刻：两个动作时间重合
senses.definition: in such a way that two or more actions happen at the same moment
senses.definitionCN: 使两个或更多动作在同一时刻发生的方式
senses.example: The lights dimmed and the music started simultaneously.
senses.exampleCN: 灯光暗下与音乐响起是同时的。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to simultaneous, so it states co-occurrence as the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 副词由 simultaneous 加 -ly 构成，因此它把共现陈述为动作的方式。

senses.title: In parallel processes
senses.titleCN: 并行推进：多项工作同时开展
senses.definition: in a manner in which several processes run side by side
senses.definitionCN: 多个过程并排推进的方式
senses.example: The team worked simultaneously on the design and the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 团队同时推进设计与预算两项工作。
senses.why: The adverb moves from a single instant to a stretch of time, describing parallel rather than point-like coincidence.
senses.whyCN: 副词从单一瞬间扩展到一段时间，描述并行而非点状的共现。

senses.title: Interpreting while speaking
senses.definition: of translation, performed while the original speech continues
senses.definitionCN: 指翻译在原话仍在进行时完成
senses.example: She translated simultaneously for three hours without a break.
senses.exampleCN: 她连续同声翻译了三个小时没有休息。
senses.why: The fixed technical phrase simultaneous interpretation produced this adverbial use, where the overlap is of voices.
senses.whyCN: 同声传译这一固定术语产生了这个副词用法，此处重叠的是两个声音。

senses.title: At once, on several fronts
senses.titleCN: 多线同时：一次动作覆盖多处
senses.definition: of an action applied to several places or targets at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同一动作在同一时间作用于多个地点或对象
senses.example: The campaign was launched simultaneously in five cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动在五个城市同时启动。
senses.why: Distribution and planning use the adverb to guarantee that no site starts first.
senses.whyCN: 发行与规划用这个副词来保证没有任何一处先开始。

senses.title: Coexisting at one time
senses.titleCN: 共处一时：两种状态同时成立
senses.definition: of states, holding at the same period
senses.definitionCN: 指两种状态在同一时期成立
senses.example: The species lived simultaneously in the north and the south.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种在南北两地同时生存。
senses.why: The adverb can describe coexistence as well as co-action: the same clock covers both.
senses.whyCN: 副词既可描述共在，也可描述共动：同一个时钟覆盖两者。

senses.title: Satisfied at once in equations
senses.titleCN: 联立成立：同组数值一并满足
senses.definition: of mathematical conditions, satisfied by the same values
senses.definitionCN: 指数学条件被同一组数值一并满足
senses.example: The two constraints must hold simultaneously.

intro.en: Simultaneously is the English adverb of simultaneous, from Latin simul 'at the same time'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: simultaneously 是 simultaneous 的英语副词，源自拉丁 simul「同时」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: The Latin adverb simul meant 'at the same time, together'. It supplied the stem but never formed a classical adverb in -e that English could borrow.
items.cn: 拉丁副词 simul 意为「同时、一起」。它提供了词干，但古典拉丁并未形成可被英语借用的 -e 副词。

items.en: The English adverb is formed inside the language by adding -ly to simultaneous. No direct Latin model exists, so the word is an English coinage.
items.cn: 这个英语副词是在语言内部由 simultaneous 加 -ly 构成的。并无直接拉丁范本，因此该词属英语自造。

items.en: The adverb appears in learned prose after the adjective, in the eighteenth century, chiefly in discussions of motion and time. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词在形容词之后出现于 18 世纪的学术散文，主要用于讨论运动与时间。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century telegraphy and twentieth-century broadcasting made the adverb routine: messages arrive simultaneously, programmes go out simultaneously.
items.cn: 19 世纪电报与 20 世纪广播让这个副词成为日常：消息同时抵达，节目同时播出。

items.en: In computing the adverb describes parallel execution, and it now appears in ordinary instructions: the two files update simultaneously.
items.cn: 在计算领域，该副词描述并行执行，如今也出现在普通说明中：两个文件同时更新。

items.en: Source uncertain (root disputed): the Latin adjective simultaneus behind the adverb is not securely explained. Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date of the adverb is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：副词背后的拉丁形容词 simultaneus 构词尚无确凿解释；来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：副词的英语首见年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds the adjective and look-alike adverbs; the second holds near-synonyms of timing.
note.cn: 第一组是形容词与形近副词；第二组是表示时间关系的近义词。

entries.definition: Modifies a noun: a simultaneous launch. The adverb modifies a verb: launched simultaneously.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰名词：a simultaneous launch。副词修饰动词：launched simultaneously。

entries.definition: Means 'without planning, of its own accord'. It comes from Latin sponte and says nothing about timing.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「未经计划、自发地」。它出自拉丁 sponte，与时间无关。

entries.definition: Means 'in an instant'. Two events can be instantaneous and still occur at different times.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「在瞬间」。两个瞬时事件仍可在不同时间发生。

entries.definition: One after another. It is the clear contrast: simultaneously overlaps, successively queues.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个。它是明确的对照：同时的重叠，相继的排队。

entries.definition: Over the same stretch of time, not necessarily at one instant. It suits long processes better than the adverb of an instant.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一段时间内，不必在同一瞬间。它比「瞬间」副词更适合长期过程。

entries.definition: Acting together in exact agreement. It stresses coordination of action, while simultaneously only stresses timing.
entries.definitionCN: 完全一致地共同行动。它强调行动的协调，而 simultaneously 只强调时间。

entries.definition: Means both 'simultaneously' and 'immediately', so it is ambiguous where precision matters.
entries.definitionCN: 既表示「同时」，也表示「立刻」，因此在需要精确处会有歧义。

entries.definition: Of processes, running independently side by side. It is common in technical writing for systems, not for moments.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程并排独立运行。它在技术写作中用于系统，而不用于时刻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: simultaneous + -ly: the adverb of one shared moment.
normal.cn: simultaneous + -ly：表示共享同一时刻的副词。

normal.en: The family runs simultaneous, simultaneously, simultaneity, simulcast.

normal.en: Fixed frames mark the senses: occur simultaneously, work simultaneously, launched simultaneously.

normal.en: The opposite adverb is successively: one after another rather than side by side.
normal.cn: 反义副词是 successively：一个接一个，而非并排。

normal.en: Watch the spelling: one m after the i, and -aneously, not -aniously.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：i 之后只有一个 m，词尾是 -aneously 而非 -aniously。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shared second: two actions land on the same instant, and the word stretches from a single moment to parallel work, overlapping voices, joint conditions and a frame-bound physical reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个共享的秒展开：两个动作落在同一瞬间，而这个词从单一时刻延伸到并行工作、重叠的声音、联立的条件与受参照系约束的物理读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pressing two switches in the same second.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在同一秒按下两个开关。

branches.en: THE INSTANT: the plainest adverbial sense, co-action at one moment.
branches.cn: 瞬间：最朴素的副词义，一个时刻的共同行动。

branches.en: THE STRETCH: parallel processes and coexisting states share a period, not a point.
branches.cn: 时段：并行过程与共在状态共享一段时间，而非一个点。

branches.en: OVERLAP AT SCALE: voices overlap in interpreting, and releases cover many cities at once.
branches.cn: 规模性重叠：同传中声音重叠，发行同时覆盖多座城市。

branches.en: JOINT CONDITIONS: equations must be satisfied together, never in turn.
branches.cn: 联立条件：方程必须一并满足，绝不能轮流满足。

branches.en: FRAME AND PERSON: simultaneity depends on an observer, and one person can do two things at once.
branches.cn: 参照系与人：同时性依赖观察者，而一个人也可以同时做两件事。

definition_en: the outer covering of a body, fruit, or liquid surface
core_image: 阳光落在手臂的皮肤上
scene: 阳光晒久了会伤害皮肤。Too much sun can damage your skin.
sceneCN: 这里 skin 是「皮肤」（第 1 个义项）；句意：阳光晒久了会伤害皮肤。

senses.title: The body's outer cover
senses.definition: the outer covering of a human or animal body
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物身体的外层覆盖物
senses.example: Too much sun can damage your skin.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光晒久了会伤害皮肤。
senses.why: This is the main everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的主要义项。

senses.title: Fruit or vegetable cover
senses.definition: the outer layer of a fruit or vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 水果或蔬菜的外层
senses.example: She peeled the skin off the apple.
senses.exampleCN: 她削掉了苹果皮。
senses.why: Plants have outer covers too.
senses.whyCN: 植物也有外层覆盖物。

senses.title: A thin layer
senses.definition: a thin layer that forms on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面形成的一层薄膜
senses.example: A skin formed on the warm milk.
senses.exampleCN: 热牛奶表面结了一层薄膜。
senses.why: Any thin surface layer can be called a skin.
senses.whyCN: 任何薄的表层都可以称为 skin。

definition_en: to hit with the flat of the hand, or to put something down noisily
core_image: 手掌快速拍在桌面上
scene: 他把书啪地放在桌上。He slapped the book down on the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 slap 是「啪地放下」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他把书啪地放在桌上。

senses.title: Hit with an open hand
senses.definition: to hit someone or something with the flat of your hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手掌平直地打某人或某物
senses.example: She slapped the mosquito on her arm.
senses.exampleCN: 她拍死了手臂上的蚊子。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: A blow or insult
senses.definition: a blow with the flat hand, or an action that feels like one
senses.definitionCN: 用平掌的一击，或让人感觉像挨了一击的事
senses.example: The refusal was a slap in the face.
senses.exampleCN: 这次拒绝是一记公开的耳光。
senses.why: The noun can name a physical or emotional blow.
senses.whyCN: 名词可以指身体的或情感的一击。

senses.title: Put down noisily
senses.definition: to put something down quickly and noisily
senses.definitionCN: 快速而带响地把某物放下
senses.example: He slapped the book down on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把书啪地放在桌上。
senses.why: The flat-hand motion extends to objects.
senses.whyCN: 平掌的动作扩展到物体上。

intro.en: Slap is probably imitative of the sound of a flat blow.
intro.cn: slap 很可能模仿平掌击打的声音。

items.en: A similar word described a flat blow.
items.cn: 一个相似的词描述平掌击打。

items.en: Slap appeared as a verb and a noun.
items.cn: slap 作为动词和名词出现。

items.en: It kept the sound of the impact.
items.cn: 它保留了撞击的声音感。

items.en: Phrases like slap on grew common.
items.cn: slap on 等短语变得常用。

items.en: It also named careless, hasty action.
items.cn: 它也表示草率匆忙的动作。

abstract.en: Haste slaps things together and calls it done.

abstract.en: The smallest contact can make the loudest sound.

definition_en: to rest with your eyes closed and mind unaware, or the state of this rest
core_image: 婴儿在摇篮里熟睡
scene: 婴儿在摇篮里安静地睡着了。The baby slept peacefully in the cradle.
sceneCN: 这里 sleep 是「睡觉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婴儿在摇篮里安静地睡着了。

senses.title: Rest with eyes closed
senses.definition: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind not aware of the world
senses.definitionCN: 闭眼休息、头脑不感知外界
senses.example: The baby slept peacefully in the cradle.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在摇篮里安静地睡着了。
senses.why: This is the basic nightly action.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的夜间行为。

senses.title: The state of resting
senses.definition: the natural state of rest in which you are not awake
senses.definitionCN: 未醒时自然的休息状态
senses.example: A good sleep can fix a bad mood.
senses.exampleCN: 好好睡一觉能改善坏心情。
senses.why: The noun names the whole state.
senses.whyCN: 名词指整个状态。

senses.title: Have room for guests
senses.definition: to have enough beds for a number of people
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的床位容纳若干人
senses.example: The small hotel sleeps twenty guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小旅馆可供二十位客人住宿。
senses.why: A building can sleep people by giving them beds.
senses.whyCN: 建筑通过提供床位让人睡下。

definition_zh: 雨夹雪；半融的雪；（美式）冰粒；下冻雨
definition_en: a mixture of rain and snow, or partly melted snow falling
core_image: 灰白的雨线里混着半融的雪，落在挡风玻璃上立刻摊成一层薄冰
scene: 雨夹着半融的雪落在挡风玻璃上，很快摊成一层薄冰。Sleet froze into a thin sheet as it struck the windscreen.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「雨与半融的雪混合落下」（第 1 个义项：雨雪混合降水）；句意为雨夹雪打在挡风玻璃上，很快冻成一层薄冰。

pos.zh: 雨夹雪；半融的雪；（美式）冰粒

collocations.phrase: a mixture of rain and sleet

derivatives.zh: 冬季混合降水（近义表达）

senses.title: Rain mixed with snow
senses.definition: a fall of rain and snow together, typical of a thaw
senses.definitionCN: 雨与雪同时落下，常见于解冻时节
senses.example: Sleet froze into a thin sheet as it struck the windscreen.
senses.exampleCN: 雨夹雪打在挡风玻璃上，很快冻成一层薄冰。
senses.why: Sleet names the halfway state between rain and snow, when flakes are melting as they fall.
senses.whyCN: sleet 命名雨与雪之间的中间状态：雪花在下落途中正在融化。

senses.title: Partly melted snow
senses.definition: snow that has begun to melt on its way down or on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在下落途中或落地后开始融化的雪
senses.example: The yard was covered in grey sleet by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到中午，院子已盖上一层灰色的半融雪。
senses.why: The same slush can be described from the snow side rather than from the rain side.
senses.whyCN: 同一摊雪泥既可从雨的一侧描述，也可从雪的一侧描述。

senses.title: American: ice pellets
senses.definition: in American usage, small ice pellets that bounce when they land
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指落地会弹起的小冰粒
senses.example: Sleet ticked against the windows all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午冰粒都在敲窗。
senses.why: American weather services use sleet for frozen pellets rather than for a rain-snow mixture, a regional split in the word.
senses.whyCN: 美国气象部门用 sleet 指冻结冰粒，而不是雨雪混合物，这是该词的地域分化。

senses.title: The glaze left behind
senses.definition: the thin ice sheet that forms when sleet or freezing rain lands
senses.definitionCN: 雨夹雪或冻雨落地后形成的薄冰层
senses.example: Sleet on the steps made the whole stairway a slide.
senses.exampleCN: 台阶上的雨夹雪把整段楼梯变成了滑梯。
senses.why: The result is named by the same word because the fall and its frozen residue are hard to separate.
senses.whyCN: 结果也用同一个词命名，因为落下与它冻成的残留难以分开。

senses.title: A driving hazard
senses.definition: sleet considered as a road condition that reduces grip
senses.definitionCN: 被视为降低抓地力的路面状况
senses.example: Sleet closed the highway for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 雨夹雪使高速公路封闭了两小时。
senses.why: Transport reports turn weather into a state of the road, and the word follows that shift.
senses.whyCN: 交通报告把天气变成路况，这个词也跟着这一转变。

senses.title: To fall as sleet
senses.definition: used as a verb meaning that sleet is falling
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，表示正在下雨夹雪
senses.example: It sleeted all afternoon and never turned to snow.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都在下雨夹雪，始终没转成雪。
senses.why: As with rain and snow, the weather noun supplies a impersonal verb.
senses.whyCN: 与 rain、snow 一样，这个天气名词也派生出无人称动词。

senses.title: A category in forecasts
senses.definition: one of the named precipitation types in a weather forecast
senses.definitionCN: 天气预报中被命名的降水类型之一
senses.example: The forecast listed sleet between rain and snow.
senses.exampleCN: 预报把雨夹雪列在雨与雪之间。
senses.why: Forecasts need discrete labels, so the continuum between rain and snow is cut into named categories.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要离散标签，于是雨与雪之间的连续过渡被切成有名字的类别。

senses.title: The sign of a thaw
senses.definition: sleet as the weather that marks the change from deep winter to thaw
senses.definitionCN: 标志严冬转向解冻的天气
senses.example: The first sleet of March told the farmers winter was ending.
senses.exampleCN: 三月的第一场雨夹雪告诉农民冬天要结束了。
senses.why: Because sleet sits at the melting point, it naturally becomes a seasonal signal.
senses.whyCN: 因为雨夹雪正处在融点，它自然成了一种季节信号。

intro.en: Sleet has no recorded Old English form and its deeper origin is uncertain. The main hypotheses are listed side by side without choosing one.
intro.cn: sleet 没有可考的古英语形式，更深来源不确定。主要假说并列列出，不作取舍。

items.en: Sleet appears in Middle English as slete, naming a mixture of rain and snow.
items.cn: sleet 在中古英语中写作 slete，指雨与雪的混合物。

items.en: No Old English form is recorded. The word is often assumed to have existed, but the assumption cannot be verified, so the Old English stage is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: 没有记录到古英语形式。人们常假定它曾经存在，但这一假定无法核实，因此古英语阶段来源不确定。

items.en: One common view connects it with Middle Low German slote 'hail' and German Schloße 'hailstone', which would make it a northern Germanic word.
items.cn: 一种常见观点把它与中古低地德语 slote「冰雹」、德语 Schloße「冰雹」联系起来，若是如此则属北日耳曼词。

items.en: Others treat it as a native formation related to the base of slush and sludge, though the sound correspondences are not clean. Neither explanation is settled.
items.cn: 另一些人把它视为与 slush、sludge 词基相关的本土构词，但音对应并不整齐。两种解释都未定论。

items.en: British usage keeps 'rain and snow mixed'; American usage specializes it to ice pellets, and both senses now appear in international forecasts.
items.cn: 英式用法保留「雨雪混合」义，美式用法专指冰粒，两种义项如今都出现在国际预报中。

note.en: Group one holds words with a similar shape but another meaning; group two holds frozen and mixed precipitation.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相近而意义不同的词；第二组是冻结与混合降水。

entries.definition: To rest with eyes closed; the vowel is the same but the final consonant is -p, and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 闭眼休息；元音相同，但词尾是 -p，意义无关。

entries.definition: A group of ships or vehicles; the first consonant is fl-, so only the rhyme is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 船队或车队；首辅音是 fl-，只共享韵脚。

entries.definition: A fine-grained rock used for roofs, or a list of candidates; the vowel is /eɪ/ and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用于屋顶的细粒岩石，或候选人名单；元音是 /eɪ/，意义无关。

entries.definition: Frozen pellets from a thunderstorm; hail is harder and more violent than sleet.
entries.definitionCN: 雷暴中落下的冻结冰粒；冰雹比雨夹雪更硬、更猛烈。

entries.definition: Rain that stays liquid in cold air and freezes on contact; it is a glaze, not a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 在冷空气中保持液态、触物即冻的雨；它形成冰壳，而不是混合物。

entries.definition: Snow and water mixed on the ground; it is the result on the pavement rather than the fall from the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 地面上雪与水混合的泥雪；它是路面上的结果，而不是从天而降的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real weather terms and real compounds, no invented etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的天气术语与真实复合词，不编造词源。

normal.en: sleet + -y = sleety, the adjective for cold wet weather with mixed precipitation.
normal.cn: sleet + -y = sleety，形容又冷又湿、夹着雨雪的天气。

normal.en: sleet shower is a real forecast phrase for a short burst of mixed precipitation.
normal.cn: sleet shower 是预报中表示一阵短促混合降水的真实说法。

normal.en: wintry mix is the broadcast term that covers sleet, freezing rain and snow together.
normal.cn: wintry mix 是气象播报中统称雨夹雪、冻雨与雪的术语。

normal.en: in British usage sleet is rain plus snow; in American usage it is ice pellets, a genuine regional split.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 sleet 是雨加雪；美式用法中它是冰粒，这是真实的地域分化。

normal.en: freezing rain differs from sleet: the rain stays liquid until it touches a cold surface.
normal.cn: freezing rain 与 sleet 不同：雨在碰到冷表面之前一直保持液态。

abstract.en: Abstractly, sleet is weather caught in transition: neither the clean crystal of snow nor the plain drop of rain.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，sleet 是正在过渡中的天气：既不是干净的雪花，也不是单纯的水滴。

abstract.en: Its identity is defined by mixture, which is why forecasts need a separate box for it.
abstract.cn: 它的身份由「混合」定义，这正是预报要为它单设一格的原因。

abstract.en: So sleet is the melting point made visible, a state that exists only while one thing becomes another.
abstract.cn: 所以 sleet 是可见的融点，是一种只在一物变成另一物时存在的状态。

examples.en: The forecast warned of sleet on the passes after midnight.
examples.cn: 预报提醒午夜后山口有雨夹雪。

examples.en: Sleet had polished the pavement into a mirror.
examples.cn: 雨夹雪把路面冻得像镜子一样亮。

examples.en: It sleeted briefly before the sky cleared.
examples.cn: 天空放晴前下了一小阵雨夹雪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「湿粒」：又湿又冷的雪粒 → sleet 雨夹雪、冰粒

root: 中古英语 slete「雨雪混合」，古英语形式无记录，更早来源不确定；一说与中古低地德语 slote、德语 Schloße「冰雹」有关，另一说与 slush 词基相关，均未定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe the halfway weather: rain mixed with snow, half-melted snow, American ice pellets, the glaze left behind, the road hazard, the verb, the forecast category and the first sign of a thaw.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述这种「半路天气」：雨雪混合、半融的雪、美式冰粒、留下的冰壳、路面危险、动词、预报类别，以及解冻的第一个征兆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: precipitation at the melting point, neither clean snow nor plain rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：处在融点的降水，既不是干净的雪，也不是单纯的水。

branches.en: MIXTURE: the same slush is described once from the rain side and once from the snow side.
branches.cn: 混合物：同一摊雪泥，一次从雨的一侧描述，一次从雪的一侧描述。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: American pellets and the forecast box are two attempts to pin down the middle state.
branches.cn: 分类：美式冰粒义与预报中的一格，是固定这一中间状态的两种努力。

branches.en: RESULT: when the mixture lands, it becomes a glaze.
branches.cn: 结果：混合物落地后变成一层冰壳。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE: the glaze turns into a closed road.
branches.cn: 后果：冰壳变成封闭的道路。

branches.en: PROCESS AND SEASON: the verb records the fall, and the timing marks the turn toward spring.
branches.cn: 过程与季节：动词记录落下，出现的时间则标志转向春天。

intro.en: Sleet is a small family: -y makes the adjective, and compound phrases name the shower, the warning and the mixed forecast.
intro.cn: sleet 的词族很小：-y 构成形容词，复合短语命名阵性降水、预警与混合预报。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor. Latin grando 'hail' and nix 'snow' are semantic neighbours, not relatives, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先。拉丁语 grando「冰雹」与 nix「雪」只是语义邻居，并非亲属，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

definition_en: thin in an attractive way, or small in amount
core_image: 纤细的身影站在窗边，姿态从容
scene: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
sceneCN: 这里 slender 是「苗条的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她身材苗条，走路却很稳。

senses.title: Thin and graceful
senses.definition: thin in a graceful and attractive way
senses.definitionCN: 以优雅好看的方式显得瘦
senses.example: She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
senses.exampleCN: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。
senses.why: This is the everyday body sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常描述身材的义项。

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: small in amount or degree, often too small
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度小，常指小得不足
senses.example: They won by a slender majority.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以微弱多数获胜。
senses.why: The thin image extends to small margins.
senses.whyCN: 「细」的意象延伸到微小的差距。

senses.title: Long and thin
senses.definition: long and thin in shape
senses.definitionCN: 形状又长又细
senses.example: Her slender fingers turned the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她纤细的手指翻过书页。
senses.why: Objects, not only bodies, can be slender.
senses.whyCN: 不仅身体，物体也可以是细长的。

intro.en: Slender is a Middle English word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: slender 是中古英语词，来源不确定。

items.en: Slendre described something thin or small.
items.cn: slendre 描述细或小的东西。

items.en: The spelling became slender.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 slender。

items.en: It praised graceful thinness.
items.cn: 它用来赞美优雅的纤细。

items.en: It also described small chances and margins.
items.cn: 它也描述微小的机会和差距。

items.en: It spread to long thin objects.
items.cn: 词义扩展到细长的物体。

note.en: Slender is compared with look-alike words and words for thinness.
note.cn: 把 slender 与形近词以及表示纤细的词作比较。

root: 中古英语 slendre，来源不确定；核心义「细而优雅」，引申为「微小、微薄」。

sensesIntro.en: Slender describes a graceful thin body, a small amount, or a long thin shape.
sensesIntro.cn: slender 形容优雅纤细的身材、微小的数量，或细长的形状。

core.en: Thinness with grace, or a margin barely there.
core.cn: 优雅的纤细，或几乎不存在的差距。

branches.en: A body keeps a fine and easy line.
branches.cn: 身体保持纤细流畅的线条。

branches.en: A win comes by a hair's width.
branches.cn: 胜利只差一根头发那么窄。

branches.en: Fingers and branches stretch long and thin.
branches.cn: 手指和枝条细长伸展。

branches.en: Body and object share the same line.
branches.cn: 身体与物体共享同一种线条。

branches.en: What is thin can still decide an outcome.
branches.cn: 纤细之物也能决定结果。
